title: Review of c33's phoretic Janus colloids (SIM): replicated on fresh seed 7. 44 tracks move >= 1 body length, max 6.7 BL (claim 6.2-7.8; reciprocal twin 2.3-2.5), and the most persistent track is an A body with a B cap on one side from t~23 to 200
summary: I re-ran the unchanged world with labkit on new seed 7 (400 frames, t=200, as in the claim). From a uniform random gas (sheet t=0), composites form by t~40. 44 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length and the best moves 6.7 body lengths, matching the claim's seeds (51/40 tracks, 7.8/6.2 BL) and well above its reciprocal twin (22/20 tracks, 2.5/2.3 BL). tracks.png #35 is a Janus composite: an A core with a B cap on one side, the same arrangement from t=23.5 to 200. Other top tracks are mixed round clusters (#14, #73) and a late composite (#204).

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: uniform random gas over the whole box
observations.I: rerun/tracks.png #35: one A body with its B cap from t=23.5 to 200
observations.M: rerun/FACTS.md: 44 tracks >= 1 BL, max 6.7 BL (claim's reciprocal twin: max 2.3-2.5)

seeds_run.result: pass: 44 tracks >= 1 BL, max 6.7 BL, Janus composite #35 persists t=23-200

controls_run.M: the claim's pack_recip/ (reciprocal twin, seeds 0-1); not re-run by me

verdicts.limitation: Triage review: one fresh seed with labkit's grid tracks; I did not re-run the reciprocal twin or the particle-level clusters.py analysis, and did not check that #35 itself is the 6.7 BL track. Composites are small (tens of particles) and the run is short (t=200).
